title: Public Sector Regulatory Corpus — FOIA & PSN
source: UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) / Cabinet Office / National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) / Public Sector Network (PSN) Authority
description: Comprehensive regulatory corpus covering UK public sector information rights (FOIA, EIR, DPA), government network security (PSN, gov.uk security standards), public sector AI procurement and deployment rules, and transparency obligations for all tiers of UK government.
key_regulations: Freedom of Information Act 2000 (FOIA) — applies to public authorities in England, Wales, NI; partially to UK-wide bodies
Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR) — applies to all public authorities across UK
Freedom of Information (Scotland) Act 2002 (FOISA)
Data Protection Act 2018 (DPA 2018) — UK GDPR implementation specific to public sector processing
UK GDPR (retained Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as amended by DPA 2018 and post-Brexit amendments)
Public Sector Network (PSN) Code of Connection (CoCo) — Version 6.0
NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) for government organisations
Government Digital Service (GDS) Service Standard — Digital Service Standard v3
Technology Code of Practice (TCoP) — Cabinet Office
Digital Economy Act 2017 — public sector data sharing provisions
Re-use of Public Sector Information Regulations 2015 (RPSI / PSI Directive implementation)
Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended) — AI procurement in government
AI in Government Deployment Framework — Office for AI / CDDO (2024/2025)
Government Security Classification Policy (GSCP)
Official Secrets Acts 1911, 1920, 1989
Civil Service Code — public duty and accountability
Equality Act 2010 — public sector equality duty (PSED) in Section 149

EU AI Act Articles relevant to public sector use: Article 6(2) — high-risk AI in public services, Article 26(10) — FRIA for public authorities deploying AI, Article 29 — registration in EU database for public sector AI use (extraterritorial if serving EU citizens)
Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (PACE) — data access and public rights
Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011 — bilingual public service obligations
compliance_requirements: FOIA Section 1 Duty: Public authorities must confirm/deny holding information and communicate information within 20 working days
FOIA Section 19 Publication Scheme: Every public authority must adopt and maintain an ICO-approved publication scheme, proactively publishing classes of information
FOIA Exemptions and Public Interest Test (Sections 21-44): Proper application of qualified and absolute exemptions with recorded PIT for each withheld request
FOIA complaints handling: Internal review within 20 working days; ICO complaint handling; First-tier Tribunal (Information Rights) appeals
EIR Article 7: Environmental information made proactively available on public registers/databases — active dissemination duty
ICO registration: Every public authority processing personal data must register with ICO (annual fee) unless exempt
DSAR handling: Subject Access Requests under UK GDPR Article 15 must be responded to within one calendar month (extendable by two months for complex requests)
Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA): Mandatory under UK GDPR Article 35 for processing likely to result in high risk — applies to all new AI/data projects
Data breach notification: Report to ICO within 72 hours under UK GDPR Article 33; notify affected data subjects under Article 34 if high risk
PSN Code of Connection: Annual compliance attestation, perimeter security standards, user authentication, malware protection, audit logging, vulnerability management
PSN annual assurance: Accredited third-party audit of network security against PSN CoCo
GDS Service Standard Assessment: 14-point assessment at alpha, beta, and live stages for all central government digital services
Technology Code of Conduct: Architecture, security, data, user-centred design, open standards, artificial intelligence (point 14 — AI-specific)
Public sector AI deployment: Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) — mandatory for all central government AI tools from 2025
Public Contract Regulations 2015: Open procurement procedure for contracts above threshold; transparency requirements for AI procurement decisions
AI in public procurement: Procurement Policy Note (PPN) on AI — transparency about AI-generated content in bids, AI impact assessment before procurement
Record keeping under Public Records Act 1958 / 1967: Document retention schedules with National Archives approval
Equality impact assessments for all new public sector policies and digital services
Accessibility Regulations 2018 (Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations): WCAG 2.2 AA or AAA for public sector websites and mobile apps
Annual data protection governance report to senior leadership (ICO accountability framework requirement)
penalties: ICO FOIA Enforcement: Practice recommendation, decision notice (binding), information notice, enforcement notice under FOIA Section 52
FOIA Section 77 criminal offence: Altering/defacing public records with intent to prevent disclosure — fine up to £5,000
ICO Monetary Penalty Notice under DPA 2018/UK GDPR: Up to £17,500,000 or 4% of annual worldwide turnover
ICO reprimand: Formal enforcement against public authorities for GDPR breaches (Section 155 DPA 2018 — monetary penalty possible for serious breaches)
High Court contempt: For non-compliance with FOIA enforcement notices — unlimited fine or imprisonment
PSN disconnection: Immediate removal from PSN for Code of Connection breach — blocks all government email, data sharing, and service access
PSN annual compliance failure: Interim compliance plan with 30-day deadline; disconnection if plan not met
Scottish Information Commissioner enforcement: Similar powers to ICO under FOISA — enforcement notices and sanctions for Scottish public authorities
Judicial review: Public law challenge to FOIA refusals/breaches — quashing orders, mandatory orders, damages for procedural breaches
AI deployment sanctions: CDDO/AI S unit can require amendment or removal of algorithmic tools that breach the Transparency Standard
Civil claims: Data subjects can claim compensation under UK GDPR Article 82 for material and non-material damage from unlawful processing
Ombudsman referrals: Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman (PHSO) or Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman (LGSCO) for maladministration in information rights handling
